units.source_text: 我突然想起夫人曾对我说过，先生有个时期非常喜欢看书，后来不知什么缘故，对于书籍不像以前那么有兴趣了。

en.t: I suddenly remembered that his wife had once told me Sensei had been very fond of reading for a time, but later, for some reason, he was no longer as interested in books as before.

units.source_text: 我把论文的事抛在一边，贸然问道：

en.t: I set the matter of my thesis aside and asked him rather rashly:

units.source_text: “先生为什么不像原来那样喜欢看书了呢？”

en.t: Why are you no longer as fond of reading as you used to be, Sensei?
There is not really a reason to speak of...

units.source_text: 大概是觉得不管看多少书，也不会有什么作为的缘故吧。

en.t: Perhaps it is because I feel that no matter how many books I read, I will not amount to anything.
Besides that, is there some other reason?
It is not exactly that there is some other reason.

units.source_text: 可能是以前吧，若是出去应酬或被人家问到，

en.t: In the past, perhaps, when I went out into company or someone asked me something,

units.source_text: 自己却没有这方面的知识，回答不出来时，便会羞愧难当。

en.t: if I did not have knowledge of the subject and could not answer, I felt unbearably ashamed.

units.source_text: 可是近来被人家问住，也不觉得多么羞愧了，

en.t: But lately, even when I am stumped by someone's question, I no longer feel all that ashamed,

units.source_text: 于是也就没有精神勉为其难地看书了。

en.t: and so I have lost the energy to force myself to read books.
In short, I have grown old.
Sensei's manner as he spoke was calm,

units.source_text: 并没有远离社会的人的那种愤世嫉俗，所以我也没有特别的感觉。

en.t: and because he did not have the bitterness of someone estranged from society, I felt nothing in particular.

units.source_text: 我虽不认为先生老了，但也并不觉得先生值得钦佩，便告辞回去了。

en.t: Although I did not think Sensei was old, I also did not find him admirable, and I took my leave and went home.
